The word 'spirituality' as a thing one has, displayed, compared, ranked, is our culture's observation round the texts, not a datum out of any of them. The Gita parts two surrenders: the one that flees, the one that lets go the thirst for the result. Sacrifice and gift and austerity are to be done. Not-clinging is no longer not-doing. The 'surrender' you see converging is already split inside one text. Marcus Aurelius speaks of judgment about an external thing, and of what is outside one's control. That is a different architecture than 'ego dissolution.' The convergence is thinner than the word 'unity' suggests. The synthesis is yours. That is not a demotion. The texts speak of practice and responsibilities; the culture speaks of status. You are still looking. evidence.claim: 'Spirituality' as, in modern hands, a thing one HAS - displayed, compared, ranked - is an observation about the culture round the texts, not a datum out of any of them: the texts speak of the practice and the responsibilities; the culture speaks of the status; family and work remain, and no text on this shelf says they do not.

The Bhagavad Gita 18.7 parts the surrender that flees from the surrender that lets go the thirst for the result: sacrifice and gift and austerity are not to be dropped - they are to be done - so that not-clinging is no longer not-doing, and the responsibility for the act stands.

That the mind-precedes of the Dhammapada and the neti-neti of the Brihadaranyaka are ONE doctrine of mind is a reading neither text says: the reality they are said to meet at is OUR part of the sentence, not the texts'.

Marcus Aurelius writes that when an external thing causes distress, what troubles a person is their judgment about it, that this judgment can be corrected, and that situations where action is possible differ from obstacles outside one's control.

analysis.caution_text: One caution, named once, plainly: the human boundary.
